summary: The proposal appears to be on the right track, with no identified problems in its structure, motivation, bibliography, figures, or schedule. Before submission, it should strengthen the specificity of its AI transparency statement and address several minor writing issues involving transitions, superlative claims, abbreviation definitions, and hyphenation.

findings.title: AI transparency statement does not specify the sections involved
findings.description: The AI transparency statement names specific tools and purposes but does not identify which proposal sections each tool was used for. Add the relevant sections explicitly, such as Abstract, Introduction, Motivation, Objective, Schedule, or Bibliography.

locations.section: Transparency in the Use of AI Tools
locations.quote: In preparing this proposal, I made use of several AI-based tools across different stages of the writing process.

findings.title: Repeated filler transitions
findings.description: Filler transitions occur repeatedly without adding substantive meaning. Remove them or replace them with direct connections between the claims.

locations.quote: Moreover, the time spent on repetitive feedback leaves less time for what matters most: helping students with their research and providing feedback on substantive topics.
Additionally, supervisors can provide feedback faster, making the process more scalable.
In addition, privacy regulations and cost require careful consideration of when to use locally self-hosted LLMs versus cloud-hosted ones.

findings.title: Unqualified superlative claims
findings.description: The proposal uses several unqualified superlative claims. Replace them with precise, evidence-based wording or explain the basis for each comparison.

locations.quote: The time spent on repetitive feedback leaves less time for what matters most: helping students with their research and providing feedback on substantive topics.
We benchmark which of these options performs best in this setting.
By building on existing processes, the integration causes the least disruption to supervisors and delivers the greatest simplification of their workflow.

findings.title: Abbreviations used before definition
findings.description: Define abbreviations before their first use. The title uses “LLM” before the abstract introduces “large language models,” and “AI” appears in the figure caption before it is defined anywhere in the document.

locations.quote: LLM Based Formative Feedback for Theses
The supervisor then revises the AI-generated draft, joins it with their own feedback, and publishes the result to the student.

findings.title: Inconsistent hyphenation of “Prompt Chaining”
findings.description: Use one form of the prompting technique consistently, preferably “prompt chaining” if it is being used as a noun phrase rather than as a compound modifier.

locations.quote: We evaluate single-prompt, prompt-chaining, and agentic setups, and assess trade-ofs between local and cloud hosting.

locations.section: Compare Prompting Techniques and LLM Models
locations.quote: Alternatives include prompt chaining and agentic setups, in which the LLM itself identifes where further lookups into the proposal are required and triggers specialized feedback generations focused on a narrower set of aspects.
• Build prototype implementations for agentic and prompt chaining setups
